desc: Decide final construction: prime-search p ≡ 1 (mod N) with exact-order element; correctness proof verified (ord_M(A) = N exactly via A^{N/q} ≢ 1 checks for all prime q | N).
Verify bounds: p = kN+1 ≤ 10^18 reachable for all N ≤ 10^9; small-N path 2^59−1 < 10^18; N=1 → (2,1) valid.
Implement deterministic Miller-Rabin for < 2^64 and fast factoring of N ≤ 10^9.
Implement k-search with small-prime prescreen and parity restriction; implement order-N element search A = pow(a, k, p) with exact-order checks.
Add per-N result caching for duplicate test cases.
Write final Python solution with fast stdin/stdout and branches: N=1 → (2,1); N ≤ 59 → (2, 2^N−1); else prime-search path.
Stress-test against brute-force verifier: all N 1..300, 200 random large N, and targeted edge classes (primes, prime powers, highly composite, near 10^9) all PASS; A, M bounds confirmed.

Measure worst-case runtime: single worst-case ~0.02 s; cached repeats instant; 10^4 mixed random cases ~6–8 s; adversarial distinct-prime load is the only slow scenario and matches intended-solution asymptotics — acceptable.

Edge review: k_max ≥ 10^9 for largest N; a-scan terminates quickly (generators of the order-N subgroup have density φ(N)/N); prescreen early-exit bug and MR base-reduction fix both applied and re-verified.
